title: What the ear hears in one frame
summary: The ear uses prosody from one 80 ms frame at 16 kHz. It starts sensing on. The point it offers is a fixed coupling, not a category list.
body:
The ear crate is ear-side prosody. One call is one 80 ms frame: 16 kHz and 1280 mono samples. That frame is the capture quantum beside the locked heartbeat. Playback stays outside this crate.

The ear starts on. A new ear senses. The default config leaves sense true, and an unset switch leaves sensing on. Closing it is an explicit deny, a config with sense false, or the off values 0, off, and deny. While sensing is off, or the purpose is workplace or education, a push is denied and the samples are not read. The pitch detector and the scalar rings drop when the switch closes. Nothing in this crate writes a file or keeps a copy of the PCM. This layer has no store, and the count of retained samples stays zero.

What the ear can hear on a granted frame is pitch in hertz, a voiced flag, voicing, energy, a speaking-rate estimate, pause, jitter, and shimmer. Voicing is the normalised autocorrelation at the period the pitch detector returned. The open-space point is a fixed coupling, not a category list. The listener offer reads valence, arousal, and strength, or nothing when one of them is non-finite. A denied frame has no offer. Push does not step the emotion core, and neither does that read. The ear can use these prosody features as the acoustic point a later listener takes. It does not publish a named category for the frame.
